A task manager for the Mac

What needs your attention rises.

Buoy keeps each task out of sight until it matters. You tell it when you want to start seeing something and when it's due. It does the rest, so the list in front of you is only what needs you now.

macOS 14 Sonoma or later Your tasks stay on your Mac
Download for Mac Source on GitHub

Free and open source. Buoy isn't notarized by Apple, so the first time you open it macOS will stop it: go to System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

The idea

Three dates, each answering one question

Most task lists mix up when something is due with when you want to think about it. Buoy keeps them apart. Use any combination, or none at all.

Show On

When do I want to start seeing this? The task waits in Upcoming until that day.

“Research landscaping ideas” shows on March 1.

Due

When does this actually need to be done? On that day it's in Today, and after it, it's overdue.

“Submit registration” is due October 15.

⌛
Lead Time

How much warning do I need? The task rises into Today this long before it's due.

“Renew passport” is due December 1 with 30 days of lead time.

How “Renew passport” moves through the calendar

Where things live

The Bridge: everything, near to far

You never file a task. Buoy looks at its dates and puts it in Today or Upcoming, and moves it on its own as the days pass. The Bridge shows it all on one page: Today first, then Upcoming, then Later. Click a heading to fold that part away.

Today

What needs your attention now. Overdue first, then due today, then anything with a deadline, then everything else.

Upcoming

What Buoy knows about but that doesn't need you yet, grouped by the day each task will rise.

Later

Tasks you've parked on purpose, so they stay out of Today until you bring them back.

Logbook

Everything you've finished, by day. Each completed round of a repeating task is kept here too.

  • Its Show On date has arrived
  • Its lead time has started
  • It's due today, or overdue
  • A snooze has ended
  • You moved it there yourself
  • It has no dates at all

Later: parked, not forgotten

Some tasks have no date and no hurry, but you don't want them in Today either. Park them in Later.

  • Park it: right-click ▸ Move to Later, press ⌥⌘L, click Later in the bottom bar, or drag the task onto Later in the sidebar.
  • Or as you type: end a quick entry with later, like Research standing desks later.
  • Bring it back with Move to Today.
  • Deadlines still win: a Later task that comes due, goes overdue or reaches its lead time shows in Today anyway.

Notes and Delegated live in their own part of the sidebar. Notes never show up in Today; projects do only when a date says so. See Notes and Delegated below.

Adding tasks

Type it the way you'd say it

Press ⌃Space in any app to open the quick entry window. Write the task in plain words and Buoy picks out the dates, lead time, repeat and tags as you type. Press Return and it tells you where the task went.

  1. 1
    From anywhere⌃Space opens quick entry over any app.
  2. 2
    In BuoyClick ＋ New Task in the bottom bar or press ⌘N. A new card opens at the top of the list.
  3. 3
    From the menu barClick the life ring in the menu bar to add a task and glance at Today.
You typeBuoy understands
Buy light bulbsA plain task with no dates. It stays in Today until it's done.
Call mom tomorrowShows tomorrow
Research landscaping show mar 1Hidden until March 1
Submit registration due 10/15Due October 15
Renew passport due dec 1 lead 30d #financeDue December 1, rises November 1, tagged Finance
Pay rent due oct 1 every monthRepeats on the 1st of each month
Gym every mon wed friRepeats on those weekdays. every weekday works too.
Book club every 2nd tuesdayThe 2nd Tuesday of each month. So do every last friday and every last day of the month.
Replace HVAC filter every 90 days after doneThe next one appears 90 days after you finish this one
Research standing desks laterParked in Later instead of Today
> gate code is 4471Not a task: a line starting with > is saved to Notes, exactly as typed

Keywords: due or by sets the due date; show, start, on or defer sets Show On; lead or warn sets lead time; every or repeat makes it repeat; #word adds a tag; later at the end parks it in Later. Dates can be today, tomorrow, a weekday, next week, weekend, in 3 days, dec 1, 12/1 or end of month. A keyword only counts when a real date follows it, so “Work on report” stays just a title.

Working a task

Open it in place

Double-click a task and it opens right there in the list. The cursor lands in the notes so you can start typing. Every change saves as you make it. Click anywhere outside the task, or press Esc, to close it.

  1. ☀
    Dates and lead timeClick Show On, Due or Lead to set them. Changing a date moves the task to the right list and tells you where it went.
  2. ↻
    RepeatDaily, weekly on chosen days, monthly on a date or “the 2nd Tuesday”, or yearly. Pick whether the next one follows the calendar or starts when you finish.
  3. #
    Tags and notesAdd tags from the tag button. Web addresses and emails in notes become links you can click.
CompleteClick the checkbox. The task is crossed out, greys, and fades into the Logbook. Click again before it's gone to change your mind, or use Undo in the message that appears (⌘Z).
SnoozeLater Today, Tomorrow, This Weekend, Next Week, or a date you pick. The task comes back on its own, and its due date doesn't change.
Move to TodayPull an upcoming or parked task in early with Move to Today in the bottom bar.
Move to LaterNot this week? Click Later in the bottom bar or press ⌥⌘L to park it.
Not nowA task with no due date that has sat in Today for two weeks says so, and offers to snooze it to next week or next month.
Rising tomorrowThe bottom of Today quietly lists what rises tomorrow. Click it to peek.
Convert to NoteTurned out it's just something to remember? Right-click the task and choose Convert to Note. Its title, notes and tags come along.
SearchClick Search in the bottom bar or press ⌘F to filter the list you're looking at.

Looking ahead

Upcoming shows when things will rise

Each task sits under the day it will come into Today, with a note saying why. Anything further out than two weeks is grouped by month.

Repeating tasks

When you complete a repeating task, it goes to the Logbook and the next one appears on its own, with the same notes, tags and lead time.

  • On a schedule: the 1st of every month, every Mon, Wed and Fri, the last Friday.
  • After you finish: every 90 days counted from when you actually did it.
  • Skip This Occurrence moves it to the next date without logging it as done.

Notes

For thoughts that aren't tasks

Sometimes you just need to write something down: a gate code, a book a friend mentioned, ideas for a meeting. Notes hold those in plain text until you copy them somewhere else, like Obsidian, an email or a doc. They never show up in Today and never send notifications.

  1. >
    From anywherePress ⌃Space and start the line with >. Wherever you'd type a task, a > line becomes a note instead.
  2. ＋
    In BuoyPress ⌥⌘N, or click New Note on the Notes screen. A blank note opens, ready to type in.
  3. ⇄
    From a taskRight-click any task and choose Convert to Note.
Plain text, alwaysNo dates, tags or formatting. #work stays as you typed it, so it becomes a tag wherever you paste it, and - bullets or **bold** come through as Markdown.
CopyHover over a note and click Copy, or select notes and press ⌘C. After copying one, Buoy offers to archive it.
Copy All & Archive⇧⌘C copies every waiting note, separated by blank lines, and archives them. Paste them into your daily note and the list is clear.
Archived, not deletedUsed notes move to Archived at the bottom of the list. Open one to copy it again or move it back. Search looks there too.
Convert to TaskRight-click a note and choose Convert to Task, or click Make Task on an open note. The first line becomes the title and the task lands in Today.
UndoChanged your mind? ⌘Z undoes archiving, deleting and converting, or click Undo in the message that appears.

Delegated

Hand the bigger things to your agent

Some to-dos are really projects: research, a draft, a comparison. Delegated is one board for handing them to an AI assistant: Shaping · Ready · In progress · Ready for review · Done. You write the brief and decide when it's ready; your agent picks it up, reports as it goes, and hands it back for you to check.

  1. 1
    Shape itClick New Project (⌘N) and write the brief. New projects start in Shaping, and nothing there is touched by your agent.
  2. 2
    Make it readyDrag the card to Ready. Ready is your agent's queue: it puts it in order and always takes the top card.
  3. 3
    Check the workYour agent moves the card to In progress with a status, then hands it in to Ready for review with what it delivered. You drag it to Done, or back for another pass.
The askThe title: what you want done, in a sentence.
Why / contextBackground, links and constraints: anything your agent needs to know.
Delivery expectationsWhat done looks like: the format, where it goes, and how you'll judge it. Your agent writes its report against this.
Save or CancelNothing changes until you click Save (⌘S). Switch to another screen mid-brief and it's still there when you come back. Esc doesn't throw it away; only Cancel does.
From your agentBelow the brief: its latest status and, once it's done, what it delivered. Saving your edits never overwrites them.
Shaping and Done are yoursYour agent can add ideas to Shaping, but only you move a card out of Shaping, and only you move finished work out of review. If it gets stuck on something only you can give it, it sends the card back to Shaping with a line saying what it needs; move it to Ready again once you've answered.
Level of effortEvery task and project can carry a rough estimate in hours, usually from your agent. It shows as a small grey ~2h on cards and an Effort chip when you open something; change it any time.
When dates matterA project with a Show On or Due date also shows up in Today and Upcoming when it's time, with a small board mark. Undated projects stay on the board.
Convert either wayRight-click a task and choose Convert to Project, or a project and choose Convert to Task. The notes become the Why / context.
Jump there⌘6 opens the board from anywhere. ⌘F filters it. Done shows the last two weeks; everything finished stays in the Logbook.

Agents

Let an assistant in, on your terms

An AI assistant or a script can add, complete, snooze, change and delete tasks and projects, work the Delegated board, and save or clear out notes, by opening buoy:// links. Buoy makes every change itself, the same way it does when you click, so nothing else ever writes to your data. No task an agent adds joins your lists until you say so.

  1. 1
    Give it the keyBuoy ▸ Settings ▸ Agent ▸ Copy Key. Every link must include it, so a web page or another app can't change your tasks.
  2. 2
    It sends linksFor example buoy://add?key=…&title=Renew%20passport&due_on=2026-12-01. Buoy doesn't even need to be open.
  3. 3
    You decideAccept and a task goes wherever its dates put it. Dismiss and it's gone. Both can be undone. Projects skip this step and land in Shaping, which is yours to review anyway.
Always markedTasks and notes an agent created show a small sparkle, and an open task says “Added by an agent”.
What it can doAdd, complete, snooze, update and delete tasks and projects, and work the board as described in Delegated. It can't complete a task you haven't accepted yet.
It can suggest whenYour agent can suggest parking a task in Later, or a day to show it or have it done, with a one-line reason. Suggestions wait at the top of Today; nothing moves until you click Accept.
It can order your workYour agent can put your todo list in order (Today follows it, and anything new sits on top until it orders again) and the Ready column, separately. Each time, Buoy says so, with Undo.
It never guessesCompleting a task by its title only works when exactly one open task has that title. Anything unclear, misspelled or missing the key is ignored, and Buoy logs why.
Review is optionalOnce you trust it, turn off review in Settings ▸ Agent and its tasks go straight to your lists. Notes from an agent always go straight to Notes.
Deletes can be undoneAnything an agent deletes is kept for 30 days in Settings ▸ Agent ▸ Deleted by agents, where you can restore it.
The detailsEvery action and option, with examples to try in Terminal, is in URL_SCHEME.md in Buoy's source folder.

Your data

Private, local, and backed up

Buoy needs no account and never sends your tasks anywhere. It works fully offline.

Stored on your MacEverything lives in one file in ~/Library/Application Support/Buoy.
Automatic backupsBuoy keeps a backup every day (the last 14), plus one before every update and every restore.
Back up and restoreFile ▸ Back Up Database saves a single file you can move to another Mac. File ▸ Restore from Backup brings it back.
NotificationsBuoy can tell you when a task rises, comes due, or returns from a snooze. Complete or snooze right from the notification. Turn each kind on or off in Settings.
Open at loginTurn it on in Settings ▸ General so ⌃Space, the menu bar and notifications keep working after a restart.
Menu barThe life ring in the menu bar shows how many tasks are in Today. Click it to add one or tick one off.
